declarations.name: Causal.Causality.PastInextensible.exists_mem_of_mem_Jplus
declarations.statement: [T1Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M] → hS : C.IsCauchySurfaceOn W S → hC : C.CausallyArcConnectedOn W → hcaus : (∀ ⦃x y : M⦄, C.le W x y → C.le W y x → x = y) → C.PastInextensible W I σ → (∃ t ∈ I, σ t ∈ C.Jplus W S) → ∃ t ∈ I, σ t ∈ S
declarations.standing: Deliverable (2), the main theorem, under the target's proposed name. These are exactly the target's hypotheses, with no tail-freeness. The curve is trimmed (exists_tailFree_retraction), stays past-inextensible over the trimmed interval (PastInextensible.of_retraction) and keeps its values (c ∘ ρ = c), so the tail-free case applies.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.PastInextensible.exists_mem_of_mem_Jplus_of_tailFree
declarations.statement: [T1Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M] → hS : C.IsCauchySurfaceOn W S → hC : C.CausallyArcConnectedOn W → hcaus : (∀ ⦃x y : M⦄, C.le W x y → C.le W y x → x = y) → C.PastInextensible W I σ → TailFree I σ → (∃ t ∈ I, σ t ∈ C.Jplus W S) → ∃ t ∈ I, σ t ∈ S
declarations.standing: The target's three cases. Write σ = γ ∘ ψ with γ inextensible (exists_subArc_of_tailFree), and let γ u be the point where γ meets S. (i) If γ u = σ t for some t, we are done. (ii) If ψ tq ≤ u, where x ≤_W σ tq and x ∈ S, then σ tq ≤_W γ u (CausalCurveIn.le_of_le). So x = γ u (IsCauchySurfaceOn.eq_of_le_of_t1_secondCountable, with hC), and σ tq = x by hcaus. (iii) Otherwise u lies below the whole of ψ '' I, because the image is ordconnected and avoids u. Then pastExtensible_of_subArc contradicts past-inextensibility.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.PastInextensible.of_retraction
declarations.statement: C.PastInextensible W I c → I₀ ⊆ I → I₀.Nonempty → I₀.OrdConnected → MapsTo ρ I I₀ → MonotoneOn ρ I → (∀ t ∈ I₀, ρ t = t) → (∀ t ∈ I, c (ρ t) = c t) → C.PastInextensible W I₀ c   (no separation axiom)
declarations.standing: What removes the tail-free hypothesis. It is the one-sided twin of the library's two-sided Inextensible.of_retraction (Causal/CExtConnexeCauchy/SubArc.lean:305), with the same proof skeleton. Both end pieces must be handled, because a past extension over I₀ has to become a past extension over I.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.PastExtensible.of_top_tail
declarations.statement: I₁ ⊆ I → I.OrdConnected → t₁ ∈ I₁ → (∀ t ∈ I₁, t ≤ t₁) → (∀ t ∈ I, t ∉ I₁ → t₁ < t ∧ c t = c t₁) → C.PastExtensible W I₁ c → C.PastExtensible W I c
declarations.standing: The constant final piece of a past extension. There is no pause. The new curve is c' ∘ (v ↦ min v (φ t₁)) over I' ∪ {v | φ t₁ < v ∧ t₁ + (v - φ t₁) ∈ I}, and the reparametrisation is φ up to t₁, then a translation. The library's Extensible.of_top_tail cannot be reused here. Its pause adds the parameters [a, a + 1] above the reparametrised image, so the image is no longer a final segment.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.pastExtensible_of_subArc
declarations.statement: I.Nonempty → C.CausalCurveIn W J γ → StrictMonoOn ψ I → MapsTo ψ I J → (ψ '' I).OrdConnected → (∀ t ∈ I, γ (ψ t) = c t) → u ∈ J → (∀ t ∈ I, u < ψ t) → (∀ t ∈ I, γ u ≠ c t) → C.PastExtensible W I c

findings: No paper label is involved: this is a programme statement, Sbierski 2312.07443's (2.4). The findings concern the target's evidence and Sbierski's text, not ETT.tex.

Tail-freeness is not needed. The main theorem holds for every past-inextensible causal curve, with no constant-tail hypothesis and no other exclusion. The trimming of exists_tailFree_retraction removes it, through PastInextensible.of_retraction (new: the library has only the two-sided Inextensible.of_retraction, SubArc.lean:305). So the question the target leaves open, 'whether the trimming removes that hypothesis, or whether a constant past tail must be excluded some other way', has the first answer.

The library's end-piece lemma Extensible.of_top_tail (Causal/CExtConnexeCauchy/SubArc.lean:185) does not preserve extensions at the past end. Its pause adds the parameters [a, a + 1] above the reparametrised image, so the image is no longer a final segment of the new interval. The constant final piece of a past extension therefore needs a different construction: append the constant through v ↦ min v a, with no pause (PastExtensible.of_top_tail). The constant initial piece takes the pause, with the initial-segment property kept on the future side (FutureExtensible.of_top_tail) and the result read through time reversal (PastExtensible.of_bottom_tail).

Deliverable (1), 'the extension form of (a)', is already in the strict library: Causal.Causality.exists_subArc_of_tailFree (Causal/CExtConnexeCauchy/SubArc.lean:422, from T-abs-c-ext-connexe-cauchy, kb/0243). A tail-free causal curve is Z ∘ ψ for an inextensible, tail-free Z, with ψ strictly increasing, continuous, with ordconnected image. The general form is exists_subArc_of_t1_secondCountable (:446). The target's evidence cites only exists_inextensible_of_t1_secondCountable and kb/0212, and its 'so (1) goes in the new module' is superseded. The module imports it and does not restate it (a restatement would be a kb/0082 duplicate). SubArc is ETT-layer and not upstream of Causal.Ladder.Rules (import_chain None), so the target's reason to keep (1) out of CurvesExtendSecondCountable is respected.

The route of the evidence is correct, with two sharpenings. (a) The 'on the curve' case is decided by values, γ u ∈ σ '' I, rather than by the parameter t_y ∈ range f. When γ u is on σ the conclusion holds whatever the parameter. (b) The 'above' case needs only u ≥ ψ tq, the parameter of the given point of J⁺, not u above the whole of range f. The 'below' case then says u lies below all of range f, which follows because the range is ordconnected and avoids u. The uniqueness in IsCauchySurfaceOn (∃!) is used only inside the acausality lemma eq_of_le_of_t1_secondCountable.

Lean ≥ Sbierski on three counts. The given point may be any point of the curve, not only its start: 'starts in I⁺(Σ, M)', sbierski2023c.txt:357. It may lie in J⁺, not only in I⁺. And the statement holds for an open W, of which M is the case W = ⊤. The I⁺ form is a corollary (exists_mem_of_mem_Iplus).

Sharpness, argued only and not formalized: in ETT both added hypotheses look necessary. In a Lorentzian spacetime with a Cauchy hypersurface, Sbierski's setting, both hold automatically. Antisymmetry: glue a ray to a circle at q, with curves going up the ray and round the circle. Then S = {y}, with y ≠ q on the circle, appears to be Cauchy. The ray is past-inextensible, q ∈ J⁺(S) along the circle, and the ray misses S. Arc-connectedness: take two timelike lines and add the non-local relations (s, 0) ≤_M (r, 1) for s ≤ 0 ≤ r + 1. They keep the curves and the Cauchy surface {0} × {0, 1} (kb/0038), and stay antisymmetric. But id over ]-∞, -1] on line 1 has the point (-1, 1) ∈ J⁺(S) and misses S. Whether each construction satisfies all of ETT's causality axioms was not checked in Lean.
questions: Sbierski's 'past inextendible' (sbierski2023c.txt:356; for a C⁰ curve, no past endpoint) is read as DEC-13's PastInextensible: no strict extension at the past end (Causal/Inextensible.lean:322). This is the library's standing reading, so nothing new is decided here. A consumer (T-abs-flrw-type step (e); Prop 2.1's (2.4) at the boundary chart) must still show that its curve σ = ι⁻¹ ∘ σ̃ is past-inextensible in the DEC-13 sense. In Thm 1.5 that is 't(σ(s)) → 0 as s → f(x₀)' (:1140).

'Causal curve' (Sbierski: past-directed causal curve; in Thm 1.5, a future-directed timelike curve) is read as DEC-6's CausalCurveIn with a future-directed parameter. A past-directed curve starting at p is that curve run backwards, ending at p. A timelike curve is a causal one. 'Cauchy hypersurface' is read as DEC-14's IsCauchySurfaceOn (every inextensible causal curve meets S in exactly one point). Both are the library's standing readings, recorded so the reading is not made silently.

'Starts in I⁺(Σ, M)' is read as 'has a point in J⁺(S, W)'. That covers both readings, the start or any point, and both I⁺ and J⁺. So nothing is decided, and the I⁺ wording is the corollary exists_mem_of_mem_Iplus.
kb_proposals: (2.4), a past-inextensible causal curve through J⁺(S, W) meets S, is Causal.Causality.PastInextensible.exists_mem_of_mem_Jplus. It holds on T1, second countable spaces, with S Cauchy in W, W causally arc-connected and ≤_W antisymmetric, and with no tail-freeness. The time reversal is FutureInextensible.exists_mem_of_mem_Jminus, Sbierski's I⁺ form is exists_mem_of_mem_Iplus, and the ladder form at M is _of_isCausal (T-abs-past-inextensible-meets-cauchy).

Constant end pieces do not affect past-inextensibility: Causal.Causality.PastInextensible.of_retraction, with no separation axiom. Extensible.of_top_tail's pause does not keep an extension at the past end. For the final piece of a past extension, append through v ↦ min v a (PastExtensible.of_top_tail). For the initial piece, use FutureExtensible.of_top_tail, which is the pause with the initial segment kept, read through time reversal (PastExtensible.of_bottom_tail) (T-abs-past-inextensible-meets-cauchy).

To place a point of an inextensible curve relative to a sub-arc: Causal.Causality.pastExtensible_of_subArc. If c = γ ∘ ψ on I and γ has a new value at a parameter below ψ '' I, then γ, cut at the top of ψ '' I, strictly extends c at the past end. Together with exists_subArc_of_tailFree, a point of an inextensible Z is either on c, above a given parameter, or below all of c (T-abs-past-inextensible-meets-cauchy).
